cards.title: Decide Open Graph image fallback (blocked on artwork)
cards.note:
REMINDER — client asked to be reminded later. Owner: client. Package B4 in the SEO/GEO plan.

No Open Graph image exists anywhere. No app/opengraph-image.*, no `images` on `/` or `/products`, no fallback. Product pages only get an og:image when the record has a hero image; the other products have none (verified live: only `test-listing` carries an image). Every share of the homepage, the catalogue and almost every product is a bare text card.

Parked on one of:
(a) client supplies brand artwork at 1200x630 (preferred);
(b) explicit decision to ship a typographic fallback built from the existing logo;
(c) explicitly accept bare text cards and drop the item.

Generating brand artwork unasked is inventing design — do not do (b) without a yes.

Also blocks: `twitter: { card: "summary_large_image" }` in the root layout, since it depends on this asset.
cards.label: Feedback

comments.content: Related to the homepage content work (k9–k32): if the homepage becomes a CMS record, an `og_image_url` field belongs on that same record rather than staying a build-time constant — so decide this one first if the artwork arrives, or the homepage table will need a second migration. `/` currently emits no `og:image` at all; `next.config.ts`'s `remotePatterns` already accepts Supabase Storage URLs, so an uploaded artwork needs no config change.

cards.title: Confirm the copy and links the control list does not cover
cards.note:
The control list covers items 1–8. These are still hardcoded marketing copy on `/` and the list does not say. Confirm each before the schema (k15) is final, because each one either adds a column or closes the door:

- **Parallax features section** — "Products that prioritizes experience & boosts efficiency", CTA "Check our product suite", 3 cards (title + description, currently over empty grey boxes, no images).
- **CTA band** — "Ask how we can help your business" + its paragraph + "Talk to an Expert".
- **Contact section** + its 4 highlights. Shared by `/`, `/products` and every product page, so if it becomes editable it needs a site-wide record, NOT the homepage one — a homepage save must not rewrite other pages.
- **Success stories heading + "Read stories" button**, and each card's href (today `#`). Item 8 asks only for the logos and images inside each card.
- **Page metadata**: `SITE_DESCRIPTION` in `lib/site.ts` is the home description and also the Organization/WebSite description in JSON-LD. Assume it stays in code unless told otherwise.
- **What item 2's CTA covers**: the hero's own button, or every "Talk to an Expert" (nav and footer are shared chrome and point at `/#contact`)?

Two more confirmations that change the form:
- Items 4 and 7 are ONE logo list — the hero strip and the marquee render the same 8 files. Confirm one editor, not two.
- Story logos are a separate list from client logos by an earlier deliberate decision. With uploads that means the same logo is uploaded twice; keep it, or let a story pick a client logo?

Acceptance: one written answer per bullet.
cards.label: Decision

comments.content: Deliberately not implemented, per the instruction not to build pushed-back scope. The /cms/home screen covers the eight controls only; the parallax band, the "Ask how we can help" band, the contact section, the story headings and buttons, the page metadata and the two dead buttons are untouched and still code. This card stays open as the written answer to "should any of those move too?" — nothing in the build depends on it.

cards.title: Verify seeded copy field by field and hand the homepage to a CMS user end-to-end
cards.note:
Code alone does not move the homepage into the CMS — this is content work, before or right after the migration deploys.

1. **PNG exports of the 8 logos.** They are SVGs in `public/` and the bucket takes PNG only: transparent background, ≈3× their rendered height (≈96–120 px tall). Same for the story logos if that list stays separate (k36).
2. **Story card images do not exist yet.** 8 images at 270×450 (upload 540×900), ≤2 MB. The overlay is designed to sit over a photograph, so placeholder greys will not do.
3. **The 9 PANDORA images** are already PNG and can be uploaded as-is (≤2 MB each). Keep the shape pairing: wide for the two wide tiles, portrait for the tall one.
4. **The hero video** — replace the Google stand-in (`EELwau9_mTA`, "Google AI Plans - Gemini Omni Version 2 9x16") with QUBE's own upload and its real accessible title. It is now a CMS edit, not a deploy.
5. **Compare every seeded field against the live `/`**: hero heading, sub-label and path, CTA, the 12 cells in the client's order, the 9 labels, "Our Clients", the stories, the video. The seed should make this a no-op; a difference is a transcription error, not a decision.
6. **Still unanswered from earlier:** whether "Lifestyle Parks" belongs back in the features grid (the "Malls" replacement was never confirmed), and what the "Learn More" / "Read stories" buttons should do.
7. Unrelated but on the same page: the existing products still have no card image, so `/products` tiles render without a picture.

Acceptance: a staff member who has never seen the code changes the hero heading and a feature cell, saves, and sees it live.
cards.label: CMS

comments.content: The code side is done; what remains is content, and the page works without it. Outstanding: PNG exports of the 8 client logos (the bucket refuses SVG, so they cannot be uploaded yet — the seeded `/public` SVG paths keep rendering until then), 8 story photographs at 540×900, and replacing the Google stand-in video link + its frame title in section 3. The 9 PANDORA tiles can be uploaded as-is. Then compare every seeded field against the live `/` and hand it to a staff user.

cards.title: Decide the homepage content boundary: what becomes editorial and what stays in code
cards.note:
DECIDED — confirmed by the client. The CMS controls on `/` are exactly these eight:

1. **Hero** — 1.1 headline; 1.2 sub-heading label + path ("QUBE Product Suite" / "Explore Our Products" → /products).
2. **Primary CTA** — label + path ("Talk to an Expert" → /#contact).
3. **Hero video** — 3.1 a video URL; 3.2 its accessible/SEO fields.
4. **Client logos** (Jollibee, KMC, ISM, …) — uploaded PNG, author resizes before upload, ≤2 MB.
5. **"Built for every businesses"** — heading + its cells (title/headline/text). FIXED at 12.
6. **"PANDORA - our most advanced Smart Locker yet"** — heading + its 9 tiles (label + image). FIXED at 9, PNG ≤2 MB.
7. **"Our Clients"** — heading + its images. "Learn More" stays as it is.
8. **Success stories** — the logo and the image inside each card.

STAYS IN CODE: SiteNav, SiteFooter, ContactSection + highlights, the parallax features section, the "Ask how we can help your business" band, story-card hrefs, both section buttons, page metadata (`SITE_DESCRIPTION` in `lib/site.ts`), and the PANDORA grid spans / slot identity.

Two relationships to keep straight: items 4 and 7 are **one logo list rendered twice** (hero strip + marquee, the same 8 files), and item 2's CTA is the hero's — the nav and footer copies are shared chrome.

What the list does not cover: k36. Imagery rules: k11 (done).
cards.label: Decision

cards.title: Decide how homepage imagery is authored (SVG logos vs. a storage bucket)
cards.note:
DECIDED — confirmed with item 4: images are uploaded through the CMS, **PNG only, max 2 MB**, and the author resizes the file before uploading. No server-side resizing, no image processing.

Consequences, all settled:
- SVG is out. The 8 client logos are SVGs in `public/` today, so PNG exports (transparent background) are content work — see k32.
- The 9 PANDORA tiles (item 6, same 2 MB cap) are already PNG and can move as-is.
- Story card images (item 8) are a new asset the client must supply; assume the same rule until told otherwise.
- `lib/media/storage.ts` allows PNG/JPEG/WebP at 5 MB for **products**. Do not widen that list or shrink that cap: the homepage gets its own constants and its own bucket (k19).
- 2 MB is well under the 6 MB `serverActions.bodySizeLimit`, so `next.config.ts` is unchanged, and `remotePatterns` already accepts storage URLs.
- `next/image` needs intrinsic size, so capture width/height at upload (`product-form.tsx` already reads a fresh file's pixels) rather than asking the author to type them.

Author guidance belongs beside each upload in the `HERO_IMAGE_NOTE` style, with the target size per slot — k23.

Also decided here: tile images and story images stay **decorative** (`alt=""`), because the label beside a tile and the logo name on a card already carry the meaning. Logo `name` is the logo's alt text and is required.
cards.label: Decision

cards.title: Decide homepage publication model and what `/` renders when the content read fails
cards.note:
Two things the singleton shape forces, both worth an explicit choice.

1. Publication. A product's `published` boolean hides a row; the homepage is one row, so hiding it would take the whole site down and a "draft" would mean duplicating every column. Recommend LIVE ON SAVE for V1: no draft state, an `updated_at`/`updated_by` stamp, and `revalidatePath("/")` from the save action. Products keep their toggle; the homepage does not get one.

2. Read failure — this is new. `/` currently performs no database read at all, so its content cannot fail. Once it reads Supabase it can, and the options differ sharply:
   a. Render an error notice (the `/products` pattern). Honest, but the storefront's main page becomes an empty shell — bad for LCP, SEO and trust.
   b. Render a typed code-level fallback identical to the seeded copy, logging whenever it is used. The site never breaks; the cost is the same copy in two places, and a test can only pin the fallback against the migration's initial seed, not against later edits.
   c. Throw to `app/error.tsx`.

Recommend (b) for `/` only, with the CMS showing the failure instead — then note the drift risk where the fallback lives.

Also settle the shape while here: one singleton table with typed scalar columns plus four typed `jsonb` arrays (business features, parallax cards, showcase tiles, clients + stories) is enough — a generic page/block builder is explicitly out of bounds per CLAUDE.md.

Acceptance: publication model and failure behaviour recorded before the migration is written.
cards.label: Decision

comments.content: Still unanswered by the control list, and still blocking k23/k25. Two questions: (a) does a save go live immediately (recommended for one row) or is there a draft? (b) what does `/` render if the content read fails? Options in the card note: error notice, a code fallback equal to the seed, or `error.tsx`. My recommendation stays: live on save, and a code fallback for `/` only, because the storefront's front page should not depend on one query succeeding.

Implemented with the recommended options, since the control list did not answer it: **live on save** (upsert on the singleton id, no draft, no publish toggle) and a **code fallback** — `lib/content/defaults.ts` is what `/` renders before the first save and again if the read fails, logging each time. The CMS reports the same failure honestly instead of pretending. Recorded as D10 in docs/DEVELOPMENT-PHASES.md §1.1 and decision 14 in CLAUDE.md.

cards.title: Add the homepage content table, RLS and a content-seeding migration (005)
cards.note:
Next migration after `004_drop_legacy_save_product_content.sql`. One singleton row: `public.homepage`, `id integer primary key default 1 check (id = 1)`.

Scalars, in the client's control order (k9): `hero_heading`, `hero_sub_label`, `hero_sub_href`, `cta_label`, `cta_href`, `video_url`, `video_title`, `video_description`, `features_heading`, `showcase_heading`, `clients_heading`, plus `updated_at` / `updated_by`.

`jsonb not null default '[]'` groups:
- `business_features` — 12 × {title, headline, text}
- `showcase_tiles` — 9 × {slot, label, image_url}
- `client_logos` — {name, image_url, width, height}
- `stories` — {name, logo_url, logo_width, logo_height, image_url}

RLS exactly as products: public read; staff read; `admin`/`editor` write via `current_user_role()`. Reuse `set_updated_at()`.

Two deliberate differences from the products schema:
- **No `save_homepage_content()` RPC.** Products need one because sections and images are child rows that must be deleted and re-inserted; here every group is a single jsonb column, so one `UPDATE` is already atomic. State that in the migration comment so nobody "fixes" it.
- **The row is seeded in this migration** (`insert … on conflict do nothing`), because it is production content, not a dev fixture like `supabase/seed/001_products.sql`. Without it `/` changes on deploy and the CMS opens empty.

Counts: validate 12 and 9 in the app (k17), not with `check (jsonb_array_length(…) = 12)`. The counts are "for the mean time", and a CHECK would need its own migration to relax; a test against the seed gives the same safety without the trapdoor.

Also: `client_logos` needs width/height for `next/image`; tile and story images stay decorative (`alt=""`).

Order: table + seed before the deploy that reads it (the 003/004 precedent).
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Define homepage content types, row mapping and validation rules
cards.note:
`lib/content/types.ts` + `validation.ts` + a `mapHomepage` mapper, modelled on `lib/products/{types,validation,repository}.ts`. (`lib/content/` is the directory CLAUDE.md's tree reserves; `lib/homepage/` is the alternative — pick one.)

Rules specific to this content:
- **Fixed counts.** 12 business cells, 9 showcase tiles: reject any payload that changes them. A 10th tile would land outside the 3×4 span map and break the grid.
- **Variable counts.** Logos and stories: cap them (8–12 is plenty) — the marquee animation and the 270 px card widths assume a small set.
- **Images.** PNG only, ≤2 MB, for logos, tiles and story images. Check the file signature, not just the MIME claim (`matchesImageSignature`). Separate constants from `MAX_IMAGE_BYTES` (5 MB, products).
- **Names are alt text.** Every logo and story needs a non-empty `name` (brand name), and `MAX_ALT_LENGTH` applies to it. Tile and story images stay decorative and must NOT be forced to carry descriptions.
- **Video.** Accept a pasted YouTube URL in its common forms (`watch?v=`, `youtu.be/`, `/embed/`, `/shorts/`) and normalise to the 11-character id; anything else is a field error. `video_title` is required — an iframe has no `alt` or `meta`, its `title` IS the accessible name and the only thing announced. If a description is wanted, it is rendered copy, not metadata.
- **Hrefs.** `/…`, `#…`, `https://…` only; refuse `javascript:` and bare hostnames.
- Trim every string, reject empty required fields, enforce per-field character limits (headline, cell text, names).
- Reordering must leave the payload complete: unique slots, no gaps.

Acceptance: pure functions with unit tests; no screen needed yet.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Add the `site-images` bucket (PNG ≤2 MB, enforced) and its upload action
cards.note:
REQUIRED — confirmed by item 4/6: uploads, PNG, ≤2 MB, author pre-resizes.

- `006_site_images.sql`: bucket `site-images`, public read, `admin`/`editor` write via `current_user_role()`, modelled on the `product-images` block in 002.
- Enforce the rule **at the bucket**, not only in the form:
  `insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types) values ('site-images', 'site-images', true, 2097152, array['image/png'])`.
  Storage then refuses an oversized or non-PNG object before any application code runs, which is the only place the rule cannot be bypassed.
- Upload action beside the product one in `lib/media/actions.ts`; bucket accessor beside `getProductImageBucket()`; a PNG-only constant group in `lib/media/storage.ts`. Do not widen or repurpose the product rules.
- 2 MB < the 6 MB `serverActions.bodySizeLimit`: no config change. `remotePatterns` already accepts the bucket.
- Logos: capture width/height at upload (`readImageSize` already does this for a picked file). SVG stays refused, so the PNG exports are mandatory (k32).
- All three image kinds — logos, the 9 tiles, the 8 story images — use this one bucket, so there is one place to look when something will not upload.

Acceptance: an editor replaces a logo, a tile and a story image end-to-end; a 3 MB PNG and a JPEG are both refused with a readable message.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Add the `/cms/home` screen and a CMS header nav entry
cards.note:
A screen the confirmed scope does not contain — the Figma set is login, product list, create, edit. `/cms/inquiries` set the precedent: added at the client's request, no frame, built from existing CMS primitives rather than a new design. Do the same and document it (k30).

Route `app/(cms)/cms/home/page.tsx`; a "Homepage" link in `components/cms/cms-header.tsx` beside "Products". The `(cms)` layout already redirects unapproved accounts; `requireEditor()` + RLS do the rest. `/cms` keeps redirecting to `/cms/products` (decision 5).

Lay the screen out in the client's own numbering — sections 1–8 — so it reads like the list they signed off:
1 Hero (headline; sub-label + path)
2 Primary CTA (label + path)
3 Hero video (URL + accessible title, optional description)
4 Client logos (list)
5 "Built for every businesses" (heading + 12 rows, fixed)
6 PANDORA (heading + 9 tiles, fixed)
7 "Our Clients" (heading only — the images are section 4's list, shown read-only with a pointer)
8 Success stories (one row per card: name, logo, image)

Read through the cookie-based client so RLS evaluates as the signed-in user, like `getCmsProducts`. Form for `admin`/`editor`; `viewer` gets the same content read-only with the existing `Notice variant="info"` copy; `isMissingRelation` produces the "apply the migrations" message rather than a stack trace.

Acceptance: an editor reaches it from the header, a viewer sees it read-only, an anonymous visitor is redirected to sign-in.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Build the homepage form and the `saveHomepage` server action
cards.note:
`components/cms/homepage-form.tsx` + `saveHomepage` in `lib/content/actions.ts`, following `product-form.tsx` / `saveProduct` rather than inventing a second idiom: `useActionState`, field errors keyed by input name, `requireEditor()` re-checked server-side, redirect with `?saved=` as a success notice, and drafts held in state so a failed save does not wipe the form.

Sections 1–8 in the client's order (k21). The repeated groups are the work:
- **4 Client logos** — add/remove/move each row, with a name (its alt text) and one PNG upload. Preview at the size it renders (~32 px tall in the marquee, ~40 px in the hero strip) so a manual resize can be judged before saving.
- **5 Business features** — FIXED 12 rows: title, headline, text. No add/remove; reorder allowed; if the count is wrong the form says so rather than dropping a row.
- **6 PANDORA** — FIXED 9 tiles: label + image. The tile's span lives in code, so name the slot's shape beside its upload ("wide", "tall", "single") and ask for a source that matches it — that pairing is exactly what `pandora-showcase-images.test.ts` protects.
- **7 Our Clients** — no editor; it points at section 4's list. Two logo editors for one dataset is how the hero strip and the marquee drift apart.
- **8 Stories** — name, logo, image, plus an href if k36 grants destinations.

Image guidance beside each field, in the `HERO_IMAGE_NOTE` idiom (the author resizes manually): logos ≈3× rendered height (≈96–120 px tall, transparent PNG); tiles at 2× (single 700×546, wide 1400×546, tall 700×1100); story card 270×450 → 540×900.

On success `revalidatePath("/")`, plus `/products` only if stories render there (k25). Do not purge every path "just in case".

Acceptance: save → error states → successful save → `/` reflects the change on the next request.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Add per-story images with the 80% black / 30% gradient hover overlay
cards.note:
New design element in item 8, not just data plumbing. Today a story card is a `bg-[#18181b]` panel with a logo centred on it and nothing else (`success-stories-carousel.tsx`). The client now wants an image in each card:

- at rest: the image sits under a **black overlay at 80%**, so the card still reads almost black;
- on **hover: the overlay becomes the brand gradient at 30%**, so the image shows through a tinted wash;
- the logo stays, drawn above the overlay.

Implementation notes:
- The overlay is one absolutely-positioned layer between image and logo (`absolute inset-0`), so `overflow-hidden rounded-[30px]` still clips the image to the card.
- The card already has its OWN hover gradient at 50% (`from-[#00c290]/50 via-[#0fb8aa]/50 to-[#1fadc5]/50`). That must be **replaced**, not stacked — two washes over the same photo darken each other and the 30% value stops meaning anything.
- Gradient stops should come from where the CTAs already define them, and the two opacities (80% rest, 30% hover) belong with the other design values rather than inline, so the pair can be tuned together.
- The card also carries `border-y-2 border-[#27272a]`; decide whether the border survives the image.

Open points: upload aspect (the card is 270×450 ≈ 0.6 — suggest 540×900 sources); whether the swap animates (the card already has a transition); and alt text — inside a link whose only text is the logo's alt, a decorative `alt=""` is defensible, but if stories ever get copy or destinations it becomes meaningful.

Acceptance: rest and hover states match the description on the client's device; no double-darkening.
cards.label: New Feature

cards.title: Read homepage content on `/` and prop-drive the shared section components
cards.note:
The read side. `lib/content/queries.ts` with the honest-failure semantics of `lib/products/queries.ts` (`DataResult`, `isMissingRelation`, one logged path); `app/(marketing)/page.tsx` becomes `async`.

Components that own their data today must take props:
- `client-logo-grid.tsx` — `CLIENT_LOGOS` becomes a prop fed by the **one** list from control 4, passed by both `hero-video-section.tsx` and `client-logo-marquee.tsx`. Do not normalise the variants' gaps, image classes or centring wrapper while doing it.
- `success-stories-carousel.tsx` — `storyCards` becomes a prop and the card gains image + overlay (k38). It also renders on `/products`: point that page at the same list (recommended) or give it a fallback, and say which.
- `pandora-showcase-grid.tsx` — labels and images from data; `id`, `variant` and `gridClassName` stay in code, and the count is fixed at 9.
- `hero-video-section.tsx` — takes `video_url` + `video_title` and derives the embed id (k17). The "no player until scrubbed into view, created paused" behaviour must survive, and the stand-in warning becomes a note about the CMS field.
- `parallax-features-section.tsx` and `businessFeatures` — not editorial unless k36 says otherwise; if the answer is "stay in code", they do not change at all.
- Metadata: `SITE_DESCRIPTION` stays in `lib/site.ts`; the JSON-LD keeps describing the business, not homepage copy.

Do not move a class. The 1px gap lines, the 30 px radii, `auto-rows-fr`, `variant="fade"`/`index={index}` and the tile spans are reasoned geometry.

Decorative `alt=""` stays on tile and story images; a logo's `name` is its alt text.

Acceptance: with the seed unchanged, `/` matches the current build apart from fixture values; a missing table produces the k13 behaviour rather than a crash.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Retarget the content-pinning tests, add new ones, and verify the build
cards.note:
Several suites read the source files and go red the moment the copy leaves the page. Plan for them:

- `tests/business-features.test.ts` — regexes cells out of `page.tsx`. Retarget the content half at the seed (or a fixtures module) and KEEP the structural half: one `h3` per cell, gap lines not borders, `auto-rows-fr`, `variant="fade"`, `index={index}`.
- `tests/client-logos.test.ts` — asserts `jolibee-logo.svg` appears in exactly two files, parses 8 literals, checks `CLIENT_LOGOS.map`. Keep the guarantees (declared once, both contexts render the shared grid, every logo has a name, 2×4 on mobile), retargeted at the data module.
- `tests/pandora-showcase-images.test.ts` — parses `cells` from the component and checks each PNG's IHDR against its tile span. With data-driven tiles the shape check reads the seed; the rule itself is still worth protecting.
- `tests/hero-video.test.ts` — pins the id and the placeholder fallback. Keep "no player until scrolled and fully in frame, created paused".

New tests: validation (12/9 equality, 2 MB PNG, href allow-list, YouTube URL normalisation), `mapHomepage` defaults, a save-wiring test modelled on `tests/product-save-wiring.test.ts`, and one pinning the story card's rest/hover overlay pair so 80%/30% cannot drift.

Run `npm test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, `npm run build`.

No browser in this workspace: the hover state, the overlay and the result of a manual resize all need the client's device. Say so rather than claiming visual QA.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Document the homepage content model, its boundary and the deploy order
cards.note:
Record what a future reader cannot reconstruct.

- `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PHASES.md` §1: the homepage is a singleton; editorial copy limited to controls 1–8; fixed 12 and 9 counts; uploads PNG-only at 2 MB enforced by the bucket; no generic block builder; publication and read-failure behaviour per k13.
- `CLAUDE.md` "Confirmed V1 Screen Scope" gains `/cms/home`, described the way `/cms/inquiries` is — added at the client's request, no Figma frame. Without this the next agent reads the route as scope creep.
- `README.md`: add `005` and `006` to the "apply in filename order" list with what they create, and state the 2 MB PNG rule. Add a bucket env var to `.env.example` only if the code gains one (the product bucket has `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PRODUCT_IMAGE_BUCKET`).
- Record the **story overlay as a client-requested addition**: 80% black at rest, brand gradient at 30% on hover. It is new visual design, in no frame, and it replaces the card's existing 50% hover gradient — otherwise someone "corrects" it back to the frame later.
- If story hrefs become editable, the "Success-story CTAs have no destination" known-gap entry becomes a content task rather than a code one.
- The stand-in warning in `hero-video-section.tsx` should point at the CMS field instead of two constants.

Acceptance: a developer new to this work can tell what is editable, what is not, and why.
cards.label: CMS

cards.title: Remove the CMS sign-in link from public chrome (nav, mobile menu, footer)
cards.note:
Client request: no sign-in affordance on the public site; `/cms/login` reachable only by typing the URL. This closes the documented open item **G15 / O3** in docs/SEO-GEO.md ("removing the `/cms/login` entry from the public footer is proposed and marked as a client-facing change"), so it is a known decision being resolved rather than new scope.

Three places expose it today, and the request needs all three, or it is still one click away:
- `components/layout/site-nav.tsx` — the desktop "Sign in" link (`accountItem`) **and** the same object passed into `MobileNav`.
- `components/layout/mobile-nav.tsx` — renders `[...items, accountItem]`, and `accountItem` is a **required prop**, so the signature has to change (drop it, or make it optional and stop rendering it).
- `components/layout/site-footer.tsx` — `accountLinks` holds `{ /cms/login, "CMS sign in" }` beside Sitemap.

Open question for the footer: once the CMS link is gone, the "Account" group holds only **Sitemap**. Keep the group as-is, move Sitemap into "Explore" and drop the second column, or rename the group? That is the only design decision here.

Consequences to state plainly: this is **cosmetic, not protective** — `/cms/login` stays public and still answers 200; access is gated by `profiles.approved`, `current_user_role()` and RLS. It is worth doing anyway: it stops spending crawl budget and internal link equity on a page that is already `noindex`, and it keeps the public chrome for customers. Staff bookmark the URL.

Docs to update with the change: `docs/DEVELOPMENT-PHASES.md` (two places still say `SiteNav` exposes `/cms/login`), `docs/SEO-GEO.md` G15 + O3 marked resolved, and the README route table note.

Verification: the three marketing routes render no sign-in link (desktop and mobile panel), the footer has no CMS entry, `/cms/login` still loads by URL, and the sign-out control inside the CMS header is untouched.
